subject: Renewal discussion — standby sidecar clusters, quota carve-outs & term adjustment
messages:
From: Claire Ortiz <claire.ortiz@aureusbiotech.com>
To: naomi.feldman@redwood.ai
Cc: procure@aureusbiotech.com
Date: 2026-07-19T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal window + new standby sidecar clusters

Hi Naomi,

We’re gearing up for our annual renewal and there are two items we need to lock in before the contract rollover on Aug 15: an isolated ‘standby’ capacity pool (for offline analytics workloads) and a small number of sidecar clusters in our VPC for regional failover. We need these to be physically isolated from our main environment for compliance (data segmentation).

High level ask:
- Add 3 standby nodes (on-prem preference) with cold KV caching enabled
- Provision 2 sidecar clusters in us-west-2 that can fail over read-only inference traffic
- 12-month term, but open to a 24-month committed pricing swap if that reduces unit cost

Attached is a short summary and our procurement contact is CC’d. Can you confirm architecture and a ballpark for the delta in recurring fees + one-time provisioning? We’ll need procurement language for SOW and an updated statement of work (SOW) to run past legal.

Thanks,
Claire Ortiz
Head of Platform Ops
Aureus Biotech

Attachment: Aureus_MAS_v3.docx (summary)
From: naomi_feldman@redwood.ai
To: Claire Ortiz <claire.ortiz@aureusbiotech.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, procure@aureusbiotech.com
Date: 2026-07-19T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal window + new standby sidecar clusters

Hi Claire — thanks for the clear ask. I’ll pull together an initial technical and commercial reply and loop in Ben for pricing. Quick clarifications from our side to size the standby pool:
- Are the standby nodes expected to serve inference traffic at any point (warm) or strictly cold/cost-optimized?
- For the sidecar clusters, do you expect write traffic to land there, or only read/failover?
- Any data residency constraints beyond us-west-2 (e.g., specific subnet or on-prem rack)?

I’ve attached a quick draft topology that maps to what you described; Karthik (cc’d) will confirm feasibility for the on-prem carve-out. We aim to get you an updated SOW + price delta by EOD Tuesday (7/21).

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Account Lead, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachment: cluster-topology-v2.drawio (draft topology)
From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: Claire Ortiz <claire.ortiz@aureusbiotech.com>, naomi.feldman@redwood.ai
Cc: procure@aureusbiotech.com
Date: 2026-07-20T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Pricing delta + term options for standby & sidecars

Claire — following Naomi’s note, high level commercial options:

Option A (12 months):
- Standby on-prem pool (3 nodes): $7,500/mo recurring + $18,000 one-time provisioning
- 2 sidecar vpc clusters (us-west-2): $3,200/mo each (recurring) + $4,000 one-time network carve-out/setup
- Total recurring uplift: $13,900/mo

Option B (24 months commit):
- 10% recurring discount on the above recurring uplift
- Waive 50% of one-time provisioning fees for standby nodes

Notes: pricing presumes standard infra residency and that sidecars are read-only unless you confirm write traffic. If the sidecars must accept writes or full KV replication we’ll need to re-run quotas and that will increase recurring costs by ~25%.

I’ll prepare a formal amendment and a draft SOW for procurement. Could we schedule a 30-min call Wednesday (7/21) at 10am PT to finalize scope?

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Looping in legal/procurement ask:
- We need Aureus to confirm the procurement contact and preferred PO cadence (net30/net45).
- Draft SOW should include an explicit data segregation appendix and acceptance criteria for the standby pool (boot time, KV cold-start behavior, and failover test plan).
- If they want on-prem racks, ops will need rack elevation drawings and a 3-week lead for on-site prep. Karthik — pls put together an ops checklist and indicate any required customer-hosted artifacts (network ACLs, jump-host IP ranges).

Thanks — Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Strategic Accounts (Renewals)
Redwood Inference
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, naomi_feldman@redwood.ai, Claire Ortiz <claire.ortiz@aureusbiotech.com>
Date: 2026-07-23T17:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing delta + term options for standby & sidecars

Claire — quick operational notes after reviewing the topology:
- Standby nodes (3) on-prem: feasible. We’ll provision them with isolated VPC peering and a dedicated HSM-backed key for encryption-at-rest. Expect ~2.5 hours of maintenance window for final cutover.
- Sidecar clusters: we can enable read-only failover without cross-region KV replication. If you later need write-accepting sidecars we recommend a write-queueing layer to avoid split-brain; that’s an additional $2,500/mo engineering ops fee.
- Required customer items before provisioning: network CIDR blocks for peering, a representative rack elevation PDF, and root contact for on-call handoff.

I’ve attached a short draft SOW with acceptance criteria and the ops checklist. If this looks good I’ll hand to field ops to schedule provisioning windows.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
